CHEK2 is a tumor suppressor gene involved in regulating cellular responses to DNA damage including DNA repair, cell cycle arrest, and apoptosis. CHEK2 activation leads to downstream activation of TP53. Loss of function mutations and copy number loss of CHEK2 are associated with cancer progression.

CDKN2A encodes two proteins, p16{INK4a) and p14(ARF), that function in regulating cell growth. The p16(INK4a) protein regulates the cell cycle through the inhibition of COK4 and CDK6, preventing them from stimulating cell proliferation. The p14(ARF) protein binds to MDM2 to keep p53 intact and stimulate the p53-dependent cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Loss of function mutations, copy number loss, and underexpression of CDKN2A are associated with cancer progression.

COKN2B encodes p15(INK4b), a protein that functions in regulating cell growth, The p15(INK4b) protein regulates the cell cycle through the inhibition of CDK4 and CDK6, preventing them from stimulating cell proliferation. Loss of function mutations, copy number loss, epigenetic variation, and underexpression of CDKN2B are associated with cancer progression.
